name: Dielectric Phase Inversion Glove DPIG-4 'Secondskin'
description:
The Dielectric Phase Inversion Glove is a full-hand wearable weapons platform that generates a controlled dielectric phase inversion field across the glove's outer surface, activated through a pressure-sensitive grip trigger integrated into the palm. On contact with a target, the field inverts the dielectric properties of whatever material it touches — organic tissue, polymer armor, composite materials — causing a rapid destabilization of molecular bonding at the contact interface. Against unprotected flesh, this manifests as a severe disruption of nerve conduction and localized cellular delamination; the sensation is described by those who survive brief contact as 'my hand stopped being my hand.' Against armored surfaces, the inversion causes surface-layer spalling and micro-fracturing that degrades protective integrity over repeated contacts.

ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC developed the DPIG-4 as part of their covert operations wearables line, specifically addressing the need for a weapon with zero ballistic signature — no projectile, no beam, no audible discharge. In a world saturated with acoustic and optical sensors, a weapon that kills through a handshake is functionally invisible to most surveillance architectures. The glove itself is visually indistinguishable from premium smart-fabric work gloves at a casual inspection; the activation hardware is embedded in the lining, and the power cell is housed in a slim cuff that passes as a fashion accessory.

The DPIG-4's weakness is its requirement for physical contact, which demands that operators be trained in close-contact engagement. ZHENG-DAO sells it exclusively through channels that require the purchaser to demonstrate certified hand-to-hand combat proficiency — a requirement that is circumvented regularly on the black market. The weapon has a disquieting cultural resonance: in GLMZ, where business deals, social hierarchies, and criminal agreements are all sealed with physical contact, the idea that a handshake could be a lethal act has entered the city's social paranoia.
tier_availability: Black market; official sales restricted to ZHENG-DAO approved contractors
legality: Prohibited — classified as an assassination device under GLMZ Covert Weapons Statute 7
specifications: activation method: Palm pressure trigger — 0.3 kg activation threshold field duration: Continuous while grip engaged power source: ZHENG-DAO FlexCell cuff battery — 40 minutes continuous use field intensity: Adjustable via thumb-dial: suppression / incapacitation / lethal weight: 180 grams (glove and cuff combined) detection: Passes standard metal detection; fails advanced bioelectric scanners recharge time: 22 minutes via standard port
tactical_use: Deployed almost exclusively in close-access covert operations: assassinations designed to appear natural, interrogations in monitored environments, and bodyguard-penetration scenarios. Operators are trained to use the suppression setting for control and compliance, escalating only when lethal authorization is confirmed. The glove's invisibility to standard security scans makes it the preferred weapon for operations inside secure facilities where ballistic weapons cannot be brought in. Some operators wear two — one set to suppression, one to lethal — on opposite hands.
cultural_context: The Secondskin has seeded a specific social anxiety in GLMZ's business and criminal elite: contact paranoia. High-value individuals have begun refusing handshakes, insisting on observed physical greetings, or wearing their own bioelectric detection rings. The phenomenon has been covered in lifestyle media as a quirky security trend, but its roots are in genuine documented cases of DPIG-4 assassinations. Ironically, ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC's own executive staff are rumored to wear detection hardware at all public appearances.
known_users: At least one documented use by a sitting mid-tier corporate executive (case sealed)
story_hooks: A prominent criminal arbitrator dies of apparent cardiac arrest during a deal. The coroner finds nothing — but a street-level fixer notices the arbitrator's hand has a faint cellular delamination pattern that matches DPIG-4 contact. Someone at that table was wearing one.

A DPIG-4 surfaces with its intensity dial removed and replaced with a fixed lethal-only circuit. The modification is clean and professional. ZHENG-DAO wants to know who performed it — because it wasn't one of their engineers.

A new bioelectric detection ring is flooding the market, supposedly able to identify an active DPIG-4 within arm's reach. The rings are real — but they're manufactured by ZHENG-DAO under a shell brand. The company is selling the antidote to its own poison.
An operator is hired to retrieve a DPIG-4 from a target who doesn't know they have it — it was planted in their belongings to frame them for a killing that hasn't happened yet.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, form-fitting smart-fabric glove that mimics premium work gloves at first glance—five-fingered, tapered, with a subtle sheen. The real weapon lies in its deceptive simplicity: it looks like something a corpo executive or skilled technician would wear. Only the slim metallic cuff at the wrist hints at its true nature, appearing as a fashionable accessory or medical device.
physical_description.dimensions: Glove length: 28 cm (wrist to fingertip); cuff width: 4 cm; cuff circumference: adjustable 16–22 cm to fit various wrist sizes
physical_description.weight_description: Exceptionally light and balanced—180 grams distributed across hand and wrist feels almost weightless in motion. The cuff is slightly heavier than the glove itself, but weight is concentrated at the wrist where it doesn't impede hand dexterity.
physical_description.primary_material: Smart-fabric composite outer layer (pressure-responsive polymer blend); embedded piezoelectric mesh beneath the surface; flexible steel-alloy internal skeleton; FlexCell battery casing in the cuff
physical_description.finish: Matte or satin finish on glove panels to avoid reflectivity; brushed titanium-grade finish on the cuff accents; surface texture varies subtly—some areas slightly raised to house activation nodes
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: charcoal gray or black with discrete undertones; Accents: brushed silver or muted rose-gold highlights on cuff controls; optional color variants in midnight blue or off-white for corpo/medical aesthetics
physical_description.grip_texture: The glove palm features a tight, almost imperceptible textured weave—grippy enough for precision work but without the obvious traction patterns of combat gear. Fingertips have a subtle raised pattern for dexterity. The cuff is smooth metal with minimal texture, designed for comfort during extended wear.
distinctive_features: Embedded thumb-dial control on the cuff (rotational, pressure-sensitive, labeled with suppression/incapacitation/lethal detents—visible only under close inspection)
Pressure-sensitive activation nodes distributed across the palm surface (invisible to the naked eye; only detectable by bioelectric scanners)

Tiny LED indicator strip along the inner wrist (dim in sleep mode, glows faintly blue when armed, shifts to amber during suppression, red during lethal mode—hidden from external view unless arm is raised)
Minimal ZHENG-DAO branding: a small 'Φ' symbol embossed subtly on the cuff, easily mistaken for a manufacturer's mark on ordinary gloves
Micro-seam detail along the knuckle ridge where piezoelectric mesh reinforces contact points
Charging port disguised as a standard smart-fabric sync connector on the inner cuff
Faint prismatic distortion across the outer surface when the field is active—visible only in certain lighting angles, like heat shimmer
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC logo appears as a discrete embossed 'Φ' symbol on the inner cuff near the charging port; a model designation 'DPIG-4' laser-marked on the cuff interior; no serial number visible on legitimate units (black-market versions often lack proper markings entirely)
physical_description.condition_typical: Field units show minimal wear due to lack of ballistic impact—gloves typically appear pristine or near-pristine. Potential degradation appears as slight discoloration on the palm from repeated activation heat, micro-scratching on the cuff from holster contact, or faint residue staining from prolonged skin contact (never truly clean after lethal use). Black-market units often show signs of hasty assembly or field repairs.
